papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has significantly influenced cancer therapy by enabling the targeting of traditionally undruggable oncogenic drivers such as transcription factors, chromatin remodelers, and mediators of protein-protein interactions, overcoming limitations of conventional inhibitors. This approach harnesses endogenous cellular machinery, specifically the ubiquitin-proteasome system and lysosomal pathways, to achieve precise and efficient elimination of pathogenic proteins. Currently, one degradation-based agent, vepdegestrant, has been approved by FDA, while most agents remain in Phase I or II evaluation, representing significant progress in addressing previously intractable targets in cancers. Nevertheless, a substantial number of disease-relevant proteins remain challenging to modulate effectively. This review focuses on undruggable targets in cancer and distinguishes three target categories: 1) Structurally undruggable targets; 2) Formerly undruggable, now inhibitor-accessible but degradation offers a mechanistic advantage; 3) Non-enzymatic targets. We highlight recent advances in the development of TPD strategies against these elusive targets to a cutoff of 30 September 2026, with the aim of providing a more systematic theoretical foundation for the broader application of the developing TPD in cancer therapeutics.

papers.abstract: Abstract The hyperactive kinase FLT3-ITD causes acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is a prognostic biomarker. We synthesized and characterized MA191 as a novel von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) E3 ubiquitin ligase-based proteolysis targeting chimera (PROTAC) for FLT3. MA191 induces apoptosis in cultured and primary AML patient cells harboring FLT3-ITD (IC 50 =9.6-11 nM; EC 50 =0.001-0.883 µM). Comparison with a VHL-binding-deficient stereoisomer of MA191 demonstrates that FLT3-ITD degradation is superior to kinase inhibition ( p < 0.03). Rapid depletion of FLT3-ITD by MA191 (DC 50 =10 nM) requires VHL, neddylation, proteasome activity, and the pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein BIM. MA191 reduces FLT3-ITD prior to apoptosis, uncovering apoptosis-independent roles of BIM for protein stability. Higher expression levels of FLT3 in leukemia cells than in healthy cells ( n = 3675/ n = 1249) are associated with worse AML patient survival ( p = 0.0099). MA191 does not harm healthy blood and bone marrow progenitor cells or myeloid cell differentiation. In Danio rerio larvae, MA191 halts AML cell proliferation without significant toxicity. Human stromal cell interactions and mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain of FLT3-ITD that confer resistance to FLT3 inhibitors do not abolish anti-leukemic effects of MA191. Accordingly, leukemia cells with acquired resistance to MA191 lack such mutations. We offer a framework for fast-acting next-generation FLT3 degraders that overcome resistance mechanisms to classical inhibitors.

papers.abstract: The bone marrow microenvironment (BME) has a significant effect on bortezomib (BTZ)-based chemotherapy in patients with multiple myeloma (MM). However, how BME components drive effective BTZ-based chemotherapy to facilitate antitumor responses has yet to be fully understood. Using single-cell transcriptome analysis, we discerned a notable increase in the density of tumor-associated IL1B+ monocytes (TAMO_IL1B), a CD14+ monocyte subcluster, within the optimal responders (OR) group compared with the suboptimal responders (SOR) group. TAMO_IL1B in the OR group had significantly greater effects on the TGF-β signaling pathway. The ligand-receptor pair (THBS1-SDC1) interaction intensity in the THBS1 signaling pathway between TAMO_IL1B and tumor plasma cells (TPC) in the OR group was significantly greater than that in the SOR group. Furthermore, pseudotime trajectory analysis indicated that TAMO_IL1B predominantly occupied late differentiation stages and was associated with a favorable response within the OR group. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for TAMO_IL1B in shaping antitumor immunity. The THBS1-SDC1 axis may contribute to interactions between monocytes and plasma cells; however, functional validation is required before any therapeutic implications can be drawn.

papers.abstract: The immune checkpoints and their inhibitors are revolutionary advances in tumour immunotherapy. Immune checkpoints, however, have a broad spectrum effect. They not only contribute to tumour immune escape, but also are involved in the regulation of the pathopathological processes of numerous inflammatory illnesses, such as sepsis, autoimmune diseases, organ transplant rejection, and viral infections, among others. Today, a considerable gap in knowledge remains regarding immune checkpoints and immune checkpoint inhibitors in non-tumour inflammatory diseases, which remains largely unaddressed. At the same time, the emergence of immune-related adverse events and resistance challenges related to the clinical use of immune checkpoint inhibitors is becoming increasingly prominent, posing a significant obstacle to their application across various diseases. To overcome such issues, this narrative review establishes a systematic framework that links immune checkpoints to various inflammatory diseases and explores the associated therapeutic and clinical challenges. These diseases pose therapeutic and clinical challenges of immune checkpoint inhibitors, which we explore. The paper not only thoroughly describes the clinical picture, pathophysiology, and interventions in immunologic adverse events but also suggests a prospective strategy to confront the existing problems with immune checkpoint inhibitors in 3 dimensions: evaluation, management, and prevention. It will attempt to present a new conceptual framework for a comprehensive understanding of the dual role of immune checkpoints (in maintaining immune homeostasis and facilitating disease progression) and to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of safer and more effective cross-disease immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, especially in relapsed/refractory patients. Aberrant PI3K/AKT/mTOR and NOTCH1 signaling converge on c-MYC to drive proliferation and ribosome biogenesis, but single-agent inhibitors targeting these pathways have shown limited clinical efficacy. Methods An FDA-approved drug library screen identified osimertinib as a candidate anti-T-ALL agent. Its efficacy and mechanism were evaluated in four T-ALL cell lines (MOLT-4, Jurkat, CCRF/CEM, and MOLT-3) with different TP53 statuses and in primary T-ALL blasts. Combination studies with selinexor, an exportin 1 (XPO1) inhibitor, were performed. Multi-omics, biochemical, and functional assays were used, and efficacy and toxicity were assessed in T-ALL xenograft models. Results Osimertinib suppressed leukemic progression in vivo by promoting proteasome-dependent degradation of c-MYC through a non-canonical, EGFR-independent pathway that cannot be fully explained by inhibition of PI3K/AKT/mTOR or NOTCH1 signaling alone. This c-MYC suppression impaired ribosome biogenesis, and combining osimertinib with selinexor further disrupted this process. The combination increased apoptosis at low concentrations (0.5-2 µM osimertinib plus 20 nM selinexor), with clear synergy at 2 µM in all four T-ALL cell lines. Mechanistically, the combination caused nuclear retention of RPS6, nuclear accumulation of RPL5/RPL11, nucleolar stress (fibrillarin dispersal), decreased MDM2 protein levels, p53 stabilization, BAX activation (6A7), cytochrome c release, c-MYC depletion, and translational suppression. In vivo, the combination improved survival and reduced leukemic burden with minimal toxicity to normal cells at low doses. Potential biomarkers include c-MYC dependency and TP53 status as candidate stratification factors, and treatment-induced c-MYC depletion and RPL5/RPL11 nuclear accumulation as candidate pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Conclusions Osimertinib plus selinexor depletes c-MYC, induces nucleolar stress, and suppresses translation, which together drive T-ALL cell apoptosis. This mechanism-driven combination shows preclinical efficacy with limited toxicity in the normal-cell and xenograft models tested. Further studies incorporating pharmacokinetic monitoring, PDX models, and prospective validation of candidate biomarkers such as c-MYC dependency, TP53 status, and RPL5/RPL11 nuclear accumulation are warranted before clinical translation.

papers.abstract: Solid tumors remain challenging for cellular immunotherapy, and CAR-T or CAR-M cells alone often have limited efficacy. Combining these approaches may improve therapeutic activity; however, our previous in vitro study observed increased IL-6, while extracellular matrix (ECM) barriers can restrict immune-cell access. We engineered IL6-CD147 CAR-M, a synthetic IL-6-responsive macrophage construct designed to couple an IL-6-binding scFv to a CD147-containing module. Following IL-6 stimulation, IL6-CD147 CAR-M showed increased MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-11, and MMP-13 transcripts and proteins. A CD147-deletion control did not reproduce the enhanced MMP transcriptional response, and GM6001 reduced CAR-T cell migration through Matrigel toward IL6-CD147 CAR-M-conditioned medium. In defined 80:20 mixed-antigen tumor models, IL6-CD147 CAR-M plus CAR-T increased tumor killing and inflammatory/cytotoxic mediators while reducing detectable extracellular IL-6. In vivo, combined therapy reduced tumor burden, prolonged survival, increased immune-cell infiltration, altered immune composition, and was not associated with overt histopathological abnormalities in the examined major organs at the assessed time points. These findings support further evaluation of an IL-6-responsive, CD147-containing CAR-M strategy; proximal receptor signaling and the mechanism underlying reduced extracellular IL-6 remain unresolved.

papers.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a well-established oncogenic driver in multiple solid tumors, most prominently in breast and gastric cancers. Beyond gene amplification-driven signaling through canonical PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK pathways, emerging evidence reveals that HER2 functions within a highly dynamic and context-dependent tumor ecosystem. Interactions between HER2-positive tumor cells and immune and stromal compartments actively shape the tumor microenvironment, contributing to immune evasion, therapeutic resistance and disease progression. A central challenge in the clinical management of HER2-altered cancers is pronounced spatial and temporal heterogeneity, which undermines both diagnostic accuracy and the durability of targeted therapies. In response, advances in multi-omics profiling, liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence-assisted analytics are redefining HER2 assessment, shifting it from static tissue-based classification towards dynamic, minimally invasive monitoring. In parallel, the therapeutic landscape has evolved from single-agent HER2 blockade to rational combination strategies. In particular, antibody-drug conjugates have emerged as a transformative modality, extending the therapeutic reach of HER2 targeting beyond traditional indications and offering new opportunities to overcome heterogeneity and drug resistance. This review synthesizes current insights into the molecular and microenvironmental biology of HER2-altered solid tumors and discusses how these advances are reshaping next-generation precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Relapsed/refractory (R/R) lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a clinical challenge with limited therapies and poor prognosis. CAR‑NK cell therapy has shown promise in solid tumors, but its efficacy is limited by both the availability of effective targets and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. CD73 (NT5E), highly expressed across solid tumors, catalyzes adenosine production to drive immunosuppression, representing both a specific CAR‑NK target and a key leverage point to overcome tumor immune evasion. However, its systematic evaluation as a therapeutically actionable target for CAR‑NK cell therapy in R/R LUAD remains unexplored. Methods We first characterized CD73 expression through integrative analysis of public datasets, primary and relapsed clinical LUAD specimens, and LUAD cell lines derived from primary and metastatic tumors. We then constructed CD73‑CAR‑NK cells and assessed their in vitro cytotoxicity across LUAD cell lines of varying malignancy, as well as their effects on extracellular adenosine and resistance to adenosine‑mediated immunosuppression. Finally, we assessed their antitumor efficacy in a stepwise manner across a tiered panel of in vivo models, including cell line‑derived xenograft (CDX), metastasis, patient‑derived xenograft (PDX), and clinically relevant immune‑humanized PDX models. Results CD73 expression was elevated in metastasis-derived LUAD cell lines and R/R LUAD specimens. Accordingly, CD73-CAR-NK92 cells exhibited potent cytotoxicity against CD73-high LUAD cells, accompanied by an activated effector phenotype, reduced extracellular adenosine, partial resistance to adenosine-mediated suppression, and limited activity toward normal bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, this enhanced function was consistently observed across multiple NK cell sources including peripheral blood-derived NK (PBNK), umbilical cord blood‑derived NK (UBNK), and iPSC-derived NK (iNK). In vivo, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, with enhanced tumor‑site enrichment, prolonged retention, and elevated intratumoral levels of TNF‑α and IFN‑γ. Importantly, in an immune‑humanized PDX mouse model, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly reduced the growth of R/R patient‑derived xenografts, accompanied by immune remodeling, without marked systemic inflammation during the observation period. Conclusions These findings provide preclinical evidence that CD73-CAR-NK cells exhibit potent antitumor efficacy for R/R LUAD through their dual functions of eliminating CD73-high tumor cells and resisting adenosine-mediated immunosuppressive signaling, supporting their therapeutic potential.

papers.abstract: For more than a century after its initial description, glioblastoma (GBM) has remained one of the most therapeutically refractory human malignancies, resembling an almost impregnable fortress against modern oncology. Despite extensive molecular characterization and identification of numerous actionable targets, survival outcomes have improved only marginally. GBM is characterized by profound spatial and cellular heterogeneity, adaptive signaling rewiring, extensive phenotypic plasticity, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and major pharmacological constraints imposed by the blood-brain barrier. This review examines the resulting disconnect between biological rationale and clinical outcome through three interrelated translational principles that determine whether mechanistically compelling therapies can achieve meaningful clinical benefit in GBM. First, who is treated and what is biologically active: therapeutic efficacy depends on matching patients to functional pathway dependencies beyond static molecular alterations. Second, whether the drug reaches and modulates its intended target: candidate therapies must achieve sufficient intratumoral exposure and demonstrate target modulation. Third, how the tumor adapts under therapeutic pressure: durable efficacy requires accounting for receptor tyrosine kinase switching, phenotypic plasticity, immune adaptation, and spatial escape. By linking these principles to the molecular, spatial, and pharmacological organization of GBM, this review frames the disease as a dynamic tumor ecosystem and provides a framework for interpreting recurrent clinical failure and guiding more biologically informed therapeutic development.

papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer with somatic POLE exonuclease domain mutations (EDMs) has a highly favorable prognosis; however, the clinical implications of non-hotspot EDMs in POLE remain unclear. In 793 patients with endometrial cancer enrolled at the National Cancer Center and Juntendo University Hospitals, 25 prespecified variants were screened using the Luminex assay. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was carried out to evaluate 54 patients with hotspot and non-hotspot EDMs. In patients with endometrial cancer (n = 4864) registered in Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange (GENIE), those harboring hotspot EDMs were matched with randomly sampled patients without EDMs, and a polymerase epsilon (POLE) score for gene panel testing was developed. In our cohort, POLE-EDMs, including hotspot (n = 91) and non-hotspot (n = 12) EDMs, were identified in 103 (12.9%) of 793 patients. The prevalence of grade 3 and advanced-stage endometrial cancer was higher in patients with non-hotspot EDMs than in those with hotspot EDMs. WES analysis of 54 patients revealed no significant differences in genomic mutations between the groups, and four non-hotspot EDMs were identified. A POLE-specific mutational signature was observed in tumors with EDM. In addition, the POLE score criteria were developed based on hotspot EDMs using the GENIE cohort, achieving a detection sensitivity of 0.94. Using the established POLE score, we identified nine non-hotspot EDMs. We identified 13 novel candidate non-hotspot EDMs using a newly established POLE score for gene panels and demonstrated an association between non-hotspot EDMs and favorable prognosis. The identification of additional non-hotspot EDMs will facilitate precise molecular classification of endometrial cancer.

papers.abstract: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide and disproportionately affects older adults. As population ageing accelerates, the global cancer burden among older adults continues to increase. This study systematically evaluated the latest global cancer burden and its epidemiological characteristics among older adults. Data on the incidence and mortality of 33 malignancies, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, among adults aged 65 + were extracted from the Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024 and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 databases and stratified by age, sex, region, and Human Development Index (HDI). Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) were calculated. Annual percentage changes (APC) were used to characterize temporal trends. Decomposition analysis was performed to quantify the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological changes. Demographic projection methods and generalized additive model (GAM) were applied to forecast the cancer burden through 2050. In 2024, there were 9,966,392 new cancer cases and 6,001,290 cancer deaths among older adults worldwide, accounting for 51.11% and 61.84%, respectively, of all-age totals. Lung, colorectal, stomach, liver, and prostate cancers were leading causes of death. Incidence and mortality were higher in men and increased with age. The Western Pacific Region had the largest burden, whereas Europe Region had the highest ASIR. ASIR correlated positively with HDI (rs = 0.771), while mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) correlated negatively (rs = -0.825). From 2000 to 2023, ASIR and ASMR declined, although burden increased, primarily driven by population growth; pancreatic cancer exhibited the most rapid increase. Tobacco use remained the leading risk factor for mortality, while metabolic risks rose in importance. Under a demographic scenario assuming constant 2024 age-specific rates and changes only in population size and age structure, new cancer cases and deaths among older adults are projected to reach approximately 19.8 million and 12.5 million by 2050, roughly double the 2024 figures, with the largest increase in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Cancer burden in older adults is substantial, varying by sex, age, region, and development level. Precision prevention and control are urgently needed, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. papers.abstract: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

papers.abstract: The systemic treatment landscape of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma has been transformed by immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens. These advances have led to efforts to combine ICIs with locoregional therapies (LRTs), particularly transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization and external beam radiotherapy, in an attempt to improve tumour control and extend the benefits of ICIs to patients with intermediate-stage disease. The rationale for this combination approach is provided by the ability of LRTs to induce immunogenic cell death and tumour antigen release and to reprogramme the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Five phase III trials have thus far shown improvements in progression-free survival and objective response rates with regimens combining ICIs with transarterial chemoembolization. Early-phase and real-world data also support the combination of ICIs with transarterial radioembolization or external beam radiotherapy, particularly in selected patients with focal disease unsuitable for embolization or portal vein tumour thrombosis. However, various challenges remain, including patient selection and therapy sequencing, response assessment, and the growing difficulties in demonstrating survival advantages in the context of widespread post-progression crossover and effective subsequent therapies. In this Review, we describe the biological rationale, summarize the clinical evidence and discuss future directions for trial design, imaging and biomarker-driven patient selection in the integration of LRTs with immune-based regimens for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.abstract: Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a subtype of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) and a rare, life-threatening complication of uncontrolled rheumatic diseases, characterized by systemic inflammation driven by aberrant activation of macrophages. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of plonmarlimab, a high-affinity neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), for the treatment of MAS. In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm clinical trial (NCT07034209 and CTR20230579), 18 patients with MAS secondary to systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease who were refractory to or had relapsed after high-dose glucocorticoid therapy were enrolled. Patients received plonmarlimab once weekly for 8 weeks at 6 mg/kg as the starting in the accelerated titration stage, and then at 10 mg/kg for the first two doses followed by dose adjustments at the investigator's discretion. The primary endpoint, overall response rate at week 8, was 83.3% (15/18) among all treated patients. The median time to response was 2.1 weeks (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.0-3.1), and the median time to remission of MAS symptoms was 1.1 weeks (95% CI, 1.0-2.3). The least-squares mean percentage reduction in glucocorticoid dose from baseline to week 8 was 79.3% (95% CI, 76.3-82.3), and 83.3% of patients (15/18) achieved a ≥ 50% reduction. No grade ≥ 3 infections were observed. Biomarker analysis showed rapid reductions in ferritin and interleukin (IL)-18 levels. Plonmarlimab showed promising clinical activity and was generally well tolerated in patients with MAS, and IL-18 may serve as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for GM-CSF antibody therapy.

papers.abstract: Late motor responses, including F-waves and H-reflexes, are commonly recorded during electrophysiological diagnostic evaluation in awake patients. Although these responses could offer added value during intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring, their use has not yet been widely adopted. This systematic review aims to assess current knowledge on how anesthetic and surgical factors influence the recording and monitoring of spinal late responses during surgery. The authors searched PubMed and EMBASE for relevant articles on studies of late response recording. Studies were considered eligible if the influence of one or more of the following parameters on late responses were assessed: (1) ventilation and metabolic parameters, (2) volatile agents, (3) intravenous agents, (4) neuromuscular blocking agents, (5) epidural or intrathecal agents, or (6) surgical factors. The QUADAS-2 tool was used to assess the risk of bias and concerns regarding applicability. Sixty-two studies were included. Respiratory conditions like hypercapnia reduced H-reflex amplitude, whereas hyperoxia and intermittent hypoxia had limited impact. Volatile agents, including isoflurane, sevoflurane, and nitrous oxide decreased late response amplitudes, with dose-dependent effects. Most intravenous anesthetics, particularly propofol, reduced H-reflex amplitude and F-wave persistence in a dose-dependent manner. Conversely, ketamine was found to increase H-reflex amplitude. During spinal and vascular surgeries, H-reflex monitoring proved feasible and provided valuable supplementary data to the conventional motor evoked potential (MEP) and somatosensory evoked potential (SSEP) modalities. This systematic review demonstrates that H-reflexes and F-waves are significantly influenced by anesthetic factors. The reviewed studies indicate that intravenous and volatile anesthetics significantly affect late responses, by reducing H-reflex and F-wave amplitudes, whereas latencies appear unaffected. The methodological quality varied significantly across the included studies and affects the interpretation of their conclusions. These findings support the potential integration of late response monitoring into intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM) protocols, provided that anesthetic management and surgical context are carefully considered.

papers.abstract: Chronic postsurgical pain after thoracoscopic surgery remains common. We investigated whether perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion would reduce chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection. In this multicentre, randomised controlled trial, 914 adults were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine or normal saline. Esketamine was administered as a 0.1 mg kg-1 bolus at induction, followed by continuous intraoperative infusion (0.1 mg kg-1 h-1) and postoperative infusion (0.015 mg kg-1 h-1) for 48 h. The primary outcome was chronic pain at 3 months, defined as persistent pain with a numeric rating scale score ≥1 during coughing in the surgical region. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, supplemental analgesics use, recovery of bowel function, in-hospital adverse events, and esketamine-related side-effects. We analysed 873 patients (median age, 55 yr; 63% female). The incidence of 3 month chronic pain was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (14.7% vs 21.2%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.62; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-0.90; P=0.013). A reduction was also observed when using a post hoc outcome definition of a numeric rating scale pain score ≥3 during coughing at 3 months (adjusted odds ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.19-0.84; P=0.015). Esketamine also reduced overall pain scores at rest and during coughing within the first 48 h, and decreased supplemental analgesic requirements within 48 h and 3 months. Perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion significantly reduced 3 month chronic pain after thoracoscopic lung resection without increasing adverse effects. ChiCTR2000040012. This trial was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Identifier: ChiCTR2000040012; principal investigator: Fu-hai Ji; dated November 18, 2020; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=62319).

papers.abstract: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability. To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines. A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel. Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied. This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

papers.abstract: State Entropy (SE) and Surgical Pleth Index (SPI) parameters aim to optimise anaesthetic depth and intraoperative opioid administration, but their impact on postoperative complications remains unclear. Insufficient training and limited decision support may contribute to inconsistent findings. Thus, we evaluated whether tailored training to improve SE and SPI compliance reduced major postoperative complications. Adult inpatients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk noncardiac surgery were included in this prospective single-centre before-after study in France. The educational intervention and outcomes were based on the Kirkpatrick framework. All anaesthesia providers were invited to participate voluntarily in lectures and bedside training on SE and SPI monitoring. Training impact was assessed using a composite of major postoperative complications within 28 days as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included changes in monitoring practices. Among 1,623 eligible patients, 1,025 were included over a 13-month period (517 before and 508 after training). Of 202 eligible providers, 91 participated in the one-month training programme (45%). After training, simultaneous SE and SPI sensor use increased from 26% to 42% (P < 0.001), and combined SE-SPI compliance increased from 23% to 39% (P < 0.001). Major postoperative complications occurred in 66/517 patients (13%) before and 71/508 patients (14%) after training (P = 0.6). Multivariable and propensity score analyses showed no significant association between the intervention and the primary outcome. This training did not reduce the incidence of major postoperative complications, despite improvements in intraoperative monitoring practices. Future educational strategies should strengthen provider engagement and reinforcement to translate improved monitoring practices into clinical benefit. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06111248.

papers.abstract: To compare ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block with transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block on recovery quality 24 h after septorhinoplasty. Prospective, randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial. Tertiary training hospital; operating room and postoperative ward. Ninety adults aged 18 to 65 years, ASA physical status I or II, undergoing elective septorhinoplasty; 89 were analyzed. After induction of general anesthesia, patients received bilateral transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block (SPG group) or bilateral ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block (IO group), 2 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine per side. Surgical infiltration and multimodal analgesia were identical in both groups. The primary outcome was the total Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 h. Secondary outcomes were QoR-15 domains, visual analog scale pain scores, rescue morphine, nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption, emergence agitation, edema, ecchymosis and recovery room stay. Total QoR-15 at 24 h was higher in the IO group (129.1 ± 9.4 versus 116.6 ± 11.7; mean difference 12.5 points, 95% CI 8.01 to 17.01; P = 0.001), above the prespecified minimal clinically important difference of 8. More IO patients crossed the acceptable symptom state threshold of 118 (86.4% versus 35.6%; P < 0.001). Pain scores were lower at every time point and fewer IO patients needed rescue analgesia (11.4% versus 53.3%; P = 0.001). Nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption and recovery room stay did not differ. Infraorbital nerve block gave better 24 h patient-reported recovery than sphenopalatine ganglion block after septorhinoplasty. Secondary findings are hypothesis-generating. papers.abstract: Indigenous Peoples in Canada are disproportionately burdened with a spectrum of health issues and consistently report lower satisfaction with their health care; nevertheless, little is known about their experiences with critical care and the support received during critical illness. We aimed to describe the current scope of critical-care-specific resources available to Indigenous patients and their families across Alberta to identify gaps and opportunities to implement actionable change to realize more equitable and culturally safe care. We conducted a two-phase environmental scan. Phase 1 entailed searching websites for information to support Indigenous patients, their families, and health care workers. Phase 2 facilitated 21 interviews with intensive care unit (ICU) stakeholders from across Alberta to further describe site-specific resources, services, tools, or initiatives to support Indigenous Peoples. Indigenous partners were engaged through all aspects of the project. Our environmental scan identified a paucity of ICU-specific resources, programs, or policies to support Indigenous patients and families' navigation with critical care. We identified two national resources aimed at clinicians, rather than patients or families. Interviews with ICU stakeholders confirmed the paucity of Indigenous-specific resources. Stakeholders cited numerous barriers, including inadequate culture training, staff time constraints and burnout, physical space limits, and insufficient personnel, such as Indigenous liaisons and social workers. Multiple gaps exist in the availability of critical-care-focused resources and supports for Indigenous Peoples experiencing critical illness in Alberta, Canada. Addressing these care gaps may improve health equity, access, and the experience for Indigenous patients and families during critical illness and further build trust and strengthen relationships with health care workers.

papers.abstract: Pain after kidney transplantation is often severe, and graft function constrains the use of systemic analgesia. Previous syntheses of regional techniques pooled them as a class, combined donors with recipients, and did not use a minimal clinically important difference (MCID). We searched PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through 5 September 2026 for randomised trials of regional analgesia in adult kidney transplant recipients (PROSPERO CRD420261478933); a trial-registry search and network meta-analysis were added post hoc. Bayesian random-effects models with MCID-scaled priors yielded posterior probabilities of benefit and of exceeding the MCID, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. Fourteen trials (903 participants) were included. Only quadratus lumborum (QL) and transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks could be pooled against control. Both yielded lower pain at every pooled time point, but no pairwise pain comparison reached 80% probability of exceeding the 1.0 point MCID. Opioid consumption at 24 h was lower with the QL block (-15.5 morphine milligram equivalents; 95% credible interval -23.6 to -6.7) and the TAP block (-10.5; -14.4 to -5.5), with each reduction exceeding the 5 mg MCID with a probability >97%. In the network meta-analysis, no difference between QL and TAP blocks in pain or opioid consumption reached 80% probability of exceeding the MCID. Graft function and safety data were too sparse to pool. Twelve eligible registered trials were unpublished; certainty of evidence was very low. Quadrtus lumborum and transversus abdominus plane blocks reduce pain and opioid consumption at 24 h, but only the reduction in opioid consumption has a high probability of being clinically important. Certainty of evidence is very low; no technique is preferred, and effects on graft function are unknown.

papers.abstract: Non-pharmacological techniques have recently been developed to decrease preoperative anxiety, and music or video may be combined, as in children. This study aims to compare two additional preoperative strategies in adult outpatients. This before-after trial was approved by the ethics committee and included adults undergoing ambulatory procedures under general anaesthesia. It compared usual care before surgery and another period with a video of the expected local journey combined with a relaxing music session. After consent, the level of anxiety was measured via the APAIS score, a repeated visual analogue scale for anxiety, and investigators collected preoperative fears. The main objective was to reduce the number of patients with significant preoperative anxiety. Secondary outcomes compared anxiety during the journey, pain, and quality of recovery after surgery. A P-value < 0.05 was considered significant. 99 patients were included in each period, and 194 completed the study. The intervention group showed a significant reduction in the rate of patients with significant anxiety at admission in the operating room: 23/95 (24.2%, 95%CI [16.7-33.7]) vs. 43/99 (43.4%, 95%CI [34.1-53.3]) with P = 0.005. Secondary outcomes showed no difference in anxiety after surgery, neither in length of stay nor incidence of PONV. The postoperative level of pain was also statistically reduced (P = 0.033). The study suggests that a combined video and music strategy decreases the rate of significant anxiety in patients undergoing outpatient procedures. This low-cost strategy showed a high level of satisfaction and should be encouraged in adults. Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT06461052.

papers.abstract: Due to limited resources, identifying high-risk surgical patients who derive clinical benefit from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission is essential. Our primary aim was to characterize resource allocation and evaluate the true clinical benefit of ICU admissions using modified Wang criteria. Secondary aim is to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission; validate clinical scoring systems; and compare inter-group outcomes, including Clavien-Dindo complication rates, lengths of stay, and mortality. This multicenter, prospective, observational study was conducted across 75 ICUs. Adult inpatient surgery cases were categorized into four groups: planned admission (PAG), unplanned admission (UPAG), planned but not admitted (PBNAG), and emergent admission (EAG). Data included preoperative/intraoperative/postoperative(ICU) variables, modified Wang criteria, and mortality rates (ICU, hospital, 30/90-day). Of 55,963 preoperatively evaluated patients, 2764 (4.9%) were planned for ICU admission; 804/2764 patients could not be admitted because of limited ICU beds, remaining of 1960 patients with a planned ICU admission, 411/1960 did not require postoperative ICU care forming the PBNAG (14.8% of 2764). Overall, 1980 patients (3.09% of all cases) were admitted to the ICU (78.2% PAG, 12.5% EAG, 9.1% UPAG). POSSUM scores effectively differentiated PBNAG (lower) and EAG (higher) from PAG. ICU benefit indicators (e.g., vasopressor need, prolonged ventilation >12 h, arrest events) were significantly higher in UPAG and EAG versus PAG (p 2 (OR 2.7) independently increased UPAG risk, whereas minimally invasive surgery and regional anesthesia reduced ICU admissions. Overall ICU and 90-day mortality rates were 5.9% and 7.5%, respectively, peaking in the EAG group (18.1% and 18.9%). Integrating modified Wang criteria, POSSUM scores, intraoperative complications, emergency status, and ASA class >2 is effective in predicting the necessity of ICU admission.

papers.abstract: Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) guide extubation decisions in intensive care unit (ICU), predicting the respiratory effort required by the patient after extubation. Different SBTs exist and should be adapted to critical illness. Viral pneumonias such as COVID-19 combine lung injury, sepsis-induced systemic inflammation, and encephalopathy, making classification challenging. The objective was to assess which SBT could be used to reproduce postextubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients. In this multicenter randomized crossover study, COVID-19-related ARDS patients mechanically ventilated at least 24 hours and ready for extubation underwent 3 different 15-minute SBT at random order: pressure support ventilation of 7-cmH2O with positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 0-cmH2O (PSV7PEEP0), PSV 0-cmH2O with PEEP 0-cmH2O (PSV0PEEP0) and T-piece trial. At baseline, end of each SBT, and 20 minutes after extubation, surrogates of respiratory effort were measured: esophageal pressure-time-product (PTPes), PTPes per minute (PTPes.min), swing esophageal pressure (SwingPes), and SwingPes per minute (SwingPes.min). Sixty measurements of respiratory effort from 12 patients were analyzed. Median PTPes.min increased from 193.8 [170.8-227.2] cmH2O.s/min at baseline to 236.6 [192.1-313.6] after extubation, with no significant differences between SBTs and postextubation. SwingPes and SwingPes.min were lower during PSV7-PEEP0 than after extubation, with median paired differences of 4.7 (95% CI 0.6-9.8) and 115.3 (95% CI 4.8-297.8), but these differences did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. No SBT modality differed significantly from post-extubation respiratory effort, suggesting that none could be excluded in COVID-19-related ARDS patients.

papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is an important postoperative neurocognitive complication, and cumulative anticholinergic drug burden (ADB) may increase its risk by impairing central cholinergic neurotransmission. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to clarify the overall association between ADB scores and POD risk in adult surgical patients. We searched major databases and trial registries through February 2026 for studies that assessed ADB using validated scales and reported POD outcomes in adult surgical patients. Random-effects models pooled SMDs and ORs. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses explored heterogeneity and robustness. Risk of bias was assessed using NOS, and evidence certainty was rated using GRADE. Ten reports from nine independent cohorts comprising 10,457 participants were included. Patients with POD had higher ADB scores than those without POD (SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.20-0.43). Each one-point increase in continuous ADB was associated with 22% higher odds of POD (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.09-1.37). Both low-to-moderate and high burden were associated with increased POD risk. In scale-specific analyses, the association was significant for ACB. The association was attenuated in studies that excluded patients with cognitive impairment. Methodological quality ranged from moderate to high, and certainty of evidence was low. Higher ADB is significantly associated with higher odds of POD, with a graded increase in risk across burden levels. Baseline cognitive impairment appears to amplify this association. These findings support preoperative ADB assessment and medication optimization in vulnerable surgical patients, while highlighting the need for prospective head-to-head comparisons of anticholinergic burden scales. papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains one of the most common serious complications after noncardiac surgery, and intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is consistently identified as a modifiable risk factor. Observational studies show a consistent, roughly dose-response association between IOH, particularly at mean arterial pressures below 60-65 mmHg, and postoperative AKI, with stronger associations in patients with limited renal reserve. Definitions of IOH vary widely, which complicates the comparison of studies and the translation of thresholds into clinical targets. Randomized trials of individualized or higher blood pressure targets have generally not confirmed a kidney-protective benefit, and pooled analyses with trial sequential analysis have not demonstrated that higher targets reduce AKI. This narrative review examines how IOH definitions evolved, summarizes the conflicting intervention evidence, and assesses the controversies that shape current practice. The review concludes that avoiding severe and sustained hypotension remains reasonable, whereas current randomized trial evidence does not support a general kidney-protective benefit of higher or individualized blood pressure targets. This conclusion is provisional and is tempered by the methodologic and causal uncertainties.

papers.abstract: Tracheal intubation is a physically and mentally demanding for anesthesiologists because it requires fine motor control, technical precision, rapid decision-making, situational awareness, and error avoidance. While videolaryngoscopes reduce muscle strain in normal airways, their ergonomic impact during difficult airway management remains poorly established. We aimed to compare upper limb muscle activity using dynamic surface electromyography during intubation via direct laryngoscopy (DL) vs videolaryngoscopy (VL) in simulated difficult airway scenarios. We conducted a randomized crossover trial involving 35 experienced anesthesiologists who performed tracheal intubation on a high-fidelity manikin with a normal airway, locked jaw, and rigid neck, respectively, using a Macintosh direct laryngoscope, a C-MAC® videolaryngoscope (C blade), and a King Vision® channeled videolaryngoscope. The primary outcome was upper limb muscle activity, measured by surface electromyography. Secondary outcomes included intubation time, force on upper incisors, first-attempt success rate, and perceived workload (National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index [NASA-TLX] score). Direct laryngoscopy produced significantly higher brachioradialis muscle activity than C-MAC VL in the simulated normal airway (16 vs 13 µV; median difference [MD], 3 µV; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0 to 5; P = 0.04), locked jaw (18 vs 12 µV; MD, 6 µV; 95% CI, 1 to 11; P = 0.02), and rigid neck (16 vs 13 µV; MD, 4 µV; 95% CI, 0 to 9; P = 0.03) scenarios. Direct laryngoscopy was the fastest method but exerted the highest force on the incisors (P < 0.001). King Vision VL was associated with the highest NASA-TLX workload score (P < 0.001 compared with DL), whereas C-MAC VL was least demanding. In simulated difficult airways, VL reduced upper limb muscle activity compared with DL. Nevertheless, perceived workload was higher with King Vision VL than with DL, whereas it was lower with C-MAC VL. Among the devices tested, C-MAC VL provided the most favorable ergonomic balance, combining reduced muscle strain, lower perceived workload, and highest first-attempt success rate across all airway scenarios. papers.abstract: Scoliosis surgery is complex and associated with significant morbidity. Accurate risk assessment is essential for appropriate resource allocation and improved care. Risk factors for developing complications have been identified; however, structured frameworks to support preoperative assessment are limited. Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) uses a three-tier multidisciplinary team (MDT) traffic-light system to triage patients based on well-defined risk factors and expert clinical judgment. We aimed to describe complications following scoliosis surgery at GOSH and evaluate the relationship between preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment and outcomes such as complication rates, operative times, and length of stay. A retrospective hospital file review was conducted for all patients presenting to GOSH for primary scoliosis surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Institutional approval was obtained, and the need for ethical approval was waived. Preoperative risk is quantified by the MDT using a three-tier traffic-light system categorizing patients as low (green), intermediate (amber), and high-risk (red). Outcomes including 30-day in-hospital complications, operative time, and length of stay were analyzed in relation to preoperative MDT traffic-light score. Of 350 eligible patients, 337 had a documented preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment. Low-risk patients comprised 43.6% (n = 147/337), intermediate-risk 49.3% (n = 166/337), and high-risk 7.1% (n = 24/337). Major complications occurred in 2% (n = 3/147) of low-risk patients compared with 50% (n = 12/24) of high-risk patients, corresponding to an adjusted odds ratio of 11.4 ([95% CI 1.98-65.4], p = 0.006). High-risk patients also had significantly longer operative times (381 min vs. 320 min, p < 0.001) and length of stay (12 days vs. 5 days, p < 0.001) when compared to low-risk patients. Patients classified as high-risk by the MDT demonstrated an increased odds of developing major complications, longer operative time, and extended length of stay when compared to low-risk patients. Similar structured tools, with local adaptations, may be valuable in other centers to support preoperative assessment, shared decision making, and guide resource allocation.

papers.abstract: Patients referred for postoperative care within enhanced care units in the United Kingdom are less likely to have their surgery canceled than those referred to critical care. Presently, it is unclear whether this association remains when examined at an individual hospital level, and whether specific structure and process features of enhanced care services influence cancelation rates within a facility. We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, observational study documenting clinical and organizational features of enhanced and critical care facilities in the United Kingdom. Features of interest included resource protections, staffing, and clinical scope. Sites with availability of both enhanced and critical care facilities, with >10 referrals to enhanced care during the study period, were selected for analysis. Cancelation rates of elective surgery within these facilities were quantified over a 3-month period between September 1, 2023, and November 30, 2023. Rates were defined as the number of elective cases canceled divided by the number of elective referrals to each facility. Multilevel regression was used to explore relationships between structure and process features of enhanced care units and surgical cancelation, using a two-level model with cases nested within hospitals to account for institutional confounding. Complete data were available for 65 sites, of which 28 had an enhanced care facility with sufficient activity for analysis, representing 4112 patients referred to enhanced or critical care. In most institutions, surgical cancelation rates were lower within their enhanced care facility than in critical care. Enhanced care units with beds reserved exclusively for elective cases (odds ratio [OR], 0.54 [0.39-0.76]; P < .001) and clinical care involving multiple specialities (OR, 0.48 [0.33-0.69]; P < .001) were associated with reduced odds of cancelation. On the other hand, enhanced care units that permitted admission of emergency cases (OR, 1.61 [1.06-2.43]; P = .024) were associated with a greater odds of cancelation. Structure and process features of enhanced care pathways are associated with cancelation rates among high-risk surgical patients in the United Kingdom. These findings may explain why cancelation rates in enhanced care are typically lower than within critical care and may have important policy implications.

papers.abstract: Preoperative anxiety affects 30% to 80 % of ambulatory surgery patients and is associated with increased anesthetic requirements, postoperative pain, and delayed recovery. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising nonpharmacological anxiolytic, but evidence remains limited in the ambulatory setting. The AMBLUMEEN (AMBulatory LUMEEN) trial is a single-center, randomized, open-label, superiority trial conducted in an adult ambulatory surgery unit. Patients with moderate-to-severe preoperative anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y-A [STAI-YA] > 45) were randomized 1:1 to standard care alone (control) or standard care and a single 20-minute preoperative VR session (immersive 360° natural contemplative scenes). The primary end point was the change in STAI-YA score from arrival in the ambulatory unit (baseline) to immediately before operating room transfer (presurgery), analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle with a linear mixed model. Secondary end points included preoperative benzodiazepine use, postoperative morphine requirement, unplanned overnight admission, patient satisfaction, and device acceptability. Of 106 randomized patients (53 per group) with a median [interquartile range] baseline STAI-YA of 49 [46-55] and 49 [46-58] respectively in the control and VR group, the VR group experienced a markedly greater reduction in state anxiety than controls. Adjusted mean between-group difference in STAI-YA change from baseline to presurgery was -18.7 95% confidence interval (CI) [-21.4 to -16.1] points in favor of VR. Although benzodiazepine requirement, postoperative pain, and unplanned overnight admission were comparable between groups, the morphine requirement in postanesthesia care unit was lower in the VR group (6/53 [11.3% 95% CI, 11.3 {4.3-23.0}] vs 0/53 [0.0%, 95% CI, {0.0-6.7}]; P = .027). Global perioperative satisfaction was high in both groups (median 8 [8-9] on 10). A single 20-minute session of medical-grade VR significantly reduced preoperative anxiety in ambulatory surgery patients, with high acceptability and an excellent safety profile.

papers.abstract: Although nonpharmacological interventions are recommended for preventing perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), cognitive training has not been explicitly advocated. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and meta-regression tested the hypothesis that preoperative cognitive training, compared with usual care, reduces the incidence of PND. Eight databases and two clinical trial registries were searched for RCTs comparing preoperative cognitive training with usual care. Primary outcomes were postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Thirteen RCTs with 1446 patients were identified. Preoperative cognitive training was associated with a lower risk of POD (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.77; P = 0.001; low certainty). Subgroup analysis (P for interaction = 0.01) and meta-regression (β1 1.072, 95% CI 0.006-2.138, P = 0.049) suggested an association between training format and treatment effect on POD, with a potentially greater benefit for traditional training. For DNR, the incidence was lower in the training group than in the usual care group (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.46-0.96; P = 0.03; very low certainty), but this finding was not supported by several sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were detected between subgroups for training format, total duration, or surgery type (P for interaction = 0.06, 0.37, and 0.34, respectively), and meta-regression suggested that overall risk of bias was a potential moderator for DNR (P = 0.045). TSA suggested a potential for false-positive findings, as the cumulative Z-curves did not cross the TSA boundaries, and the required information sizes were not reached for either outcome. Preoperative cognitive training may reduce the incidence of POD, with traditional training showing a potentially greater benefit than digital training. For DNR, the current evidence is insufficient to support a preventive effect of preoperative cognitive training, although a trend toward benefit was observed. These findings are limited by high risk of bias in several included trials and failure to reach the required information sizes in TSA, particularly for DNR, which need to be confirmed in future large-scale RCTs. papers.abstract: Inflammation is widely viewed as a driver of pain, yet clinical and transcriptomic studies report conflicting associations. A clearer understanding of how inflammatory processes relate to pain across clinical contexts is essential for improving diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of chronic pain. We analysed whole-blood RNA sequencing from seven human cohorts spanning four pain conditions, including acute, postoperative, chronic localised, and chronic widespread pain in almost 500 blood samples with corresponding pain intensity scores. Using gene-level meta-analyses, pathway enrichment, and immune cell-specific gene ontologies, we tested how inflammatory responses relate to current pain, future pain trajectories, and within-person changes over time. Inflammation emerged as one of the strongest biological correlates of pain across all cohorts, yet its association direction depended on the pain state. In acute musculoskeletal and postoperative pain, higher inflammatory activation, which correlated with enhanced neutrophil and macrophage function, was associated with greater pain intensity but also correlated with better subsequent recovery, consistent with an adaptive inflammatory response. In chronic localised pain, this relationship was disrupted and inverted: higher inflammatory activity was linked to lower pain intensity and associated with worse long-term outcomes. In chronic widespread pain, macrophage-related inflammatory activity remained positively associated with both pain severity and persistence, suggesting progression toward a maladaptive immune state. These findings indicate that inflammation is not uniformly detrimental in pain but plays distinct roles depending on disease stage and context. Inflammation might support resolution during acute injury yet become dysregulated in chronic and nociplastic pain. Recognising these context-dependent roles could help explain conflicting findings in the literature and guide more precise use of anti-inflammatory therapies.

papers.abstract: Pre-operative clear fluid fasting in children aims to reduce the risk of pulmonary aspiration. Recent studies have shown the safety of shorter clear fluid fasting durations. However, because pulmonary aspiration is rare, it remains uncertain whether the incidence differs between the liberal (< 2 h) and conventional (≥ 2 h) clear fluid fasting policies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, performing comprehensive searches across five databases. We included studies with patients aged < 18 y who underwent general anaesthesia or sedation for surgery or procedures. Primary outcome was pulmonary aspiration and secondary outcome was vomiting without pulmonary aspiration. We performed meta-analyses to estimate pooled incidences according to fasting policy (< 2 h vs. ≥ 2 h). We included 33 studies involving 580,197 patients. Twenty-nine studies (579,737 patients) reported pulmonary aspiration. The pooled incidence of pulmonary aspiration was 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with conventional fasting policies and 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with liberal policies. Risk ratios were available from 14 studies (475,399 patients) and showed no difference in pulmonary aspiration between policies (risk ratio 0.77, 95%CI 0.40-1.47). Seventeen studies (344,653 patients) reported vomiting; the pooled incidence was 0.99% (95%CI 0.27-3.51%) with conventional policies and 0.76% (95%CI 0.18-3.14%) with liberal policies. The certainty of evidence was very low for both outcomes. Pulmonary aspiration is rare in children, and similar incidences of aspiration and vomiting were observed under liberal and conventional clear fluid fasting policies. The results should be interpreted cautiously due to the very low certainty of evidence.

papers.abstract: During sevoflurane-induced anesthesia, electroencephalography analysis demonstrates alpha oscillations shifting from the occipital to the frontal regions, with further characteristic changes during maintenance and emergence. We aimed to exploratorily investigate whether alterations in alpha anteriorization and functional network efficiency are associated with postoperative delirium. This prospective, exploratory observational study enrolled 100 patients from a single tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into nondelirium (n = 81) and delirium (n = 19) groups based on delirium assessments. After excluding 17 patients due to artifacts on electroencephalography, 19-channel electroencephalography data were collected from 83 elderly patients under sevoflurane-induced anesthesia. Artifact-free epochs were extracted during the induction, maintenance, emergence, and postanesthesia care unit phases. Spectral, topographical, and network analyses were conducted. Postoperative delirium was assessed using confusion assessment method for intensive care unit and a chart review. Significant group differences emerged just before the loss of responsiveness, with the nondelirium group exhibiting robust alpha power amplification across all brain regions (median [interquartile range {IQR}] in dB; frontal: 4.24 [1.86-6.57] vs -0.88 [-1.59-3.38], P = .007; parietal: 3.71 [0.51-5.55] vs -0.95 [-2.33-1.11], P = .046; occipital: 2.81 [0.49-5.71] vs -0.04 [-2.06-1.27], P = .048), whereas the delirium group showed minimal changes. During the maintenance phase, spectral analysis revealed higher alpha power in the nondelirium group across all 19 channels (frontal: 5.42 [2.90-8.16] vs 2.89 [-0.03-5.09], P = .007; 18 of 19 channels significant by false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected permutation test). Network analysis demonstrated longer averaged characteristic path lengths in the delirium group (mean ± standard deviation [SD], 4.49 ± 0.62 vs 3.57 ± 0.16, P = .026, FDR-corrected), consistently in the frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, suggesting reduced network efficiency. Delirium was associated with early disruption of alpha anteriorization during induction and globally reduced functional network efficiency during maintenance. Perioperative electroencephalogram (EEG) transition features may serve as early markers of delirium susceptibility.

papers.abstract: Anesthetic management in general surgery poses substantial risks in elderly patients because age-related physiologic decline and preexisting comorbidities increase vulnerability to peri-operative complications. Older adults have reduced physiological reserve, impaired organ function, and slower recovery from surgical and anesthetic stress, placing them at increased risk for postoperative delirium and early postoperative cognitive impairment. Dexmedetomidine, a selective α2-adrenergic receptor agonist, has sedative, anti-inflammatory, and opioid-sparing properties that may influence early postoperative cognitive outcomes without significant respiratory depression. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between dexmedetomidine and 24-h postoperative delirium/early postoperative cognitive impairment in elderly patients undergoing general surgery. Four studies involving 479 patients met the inclusion criteria. Across the included studies, dexmedetomidine was generally administered as a 1 µg/kg loading dose followed by continuous intraoperative maintenance infusion of 0.2-0.7 µg/kg/h. Pooled analysis showed that dexmedetomidine was associated with significantly lower odds of 24-h postoperative delirium/early postoperative cognitive impairment compared with control treatment (pooled OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.24-0.61; p < 0.001). These findings suggest that dexmedetomidine is associated with lower odds of early postoperative cognitive outcomes in elderly surgical patients compared with control treatment. Larger, long-term studies are needed to confirm these findings and establish standardized dosing protocols.

papers.abstract: Total shoulder arthroplasty is associated with moderate-to-severe postoperative pain. The aim of this systematic review was to assess the available literature and provide PROSPECT (PROcedure SPECific Postoperative Pain ManagemenT) recommendations for optimal pain management after total shoulder arthroplasty. A systematic review utilising PROSPECT methodology was performed. Randomised controlled trials and systematic reviews published in the English language that assessed postoperative pain using analgesic, anaesthetic and surgical interventions were identified from databases. Of the 1809 articles identified, 30 randomised controlled trials and seven systematic reviews/meta-analyses met our inclusion criteria. Interventions that improved postoperative pain relief included: paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; dexamethasone; interscalene brachial plexus block and, as an alternative, local infiltration analgesia. Conflicting evidence was found for continuous interscalene brachial plexus block (catheter) or liposomal bupivacaine for interscalene block or local infiltration analgesia. No evidence was found for a specific surgical technique. In the absence of contraindication, the analgesic regimen should include: paracetamol; a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug administered peri-operatively and continued postoperatively; intravenous dexamethasone (8-10 mg); and postoperative opioids for rescue analgesia. As a regional technique, an interscalene brachial plexus block with a single-bolus injection of long-acting local anaesthetic (bupivacaine or ropivacaine), but not liposomal bupivacaine, should be provided. In case of contraindications or absence of expertise, local infiltration analgesia is a reasonable alternative. Further studies are required to investigate the analgesic benefit of a continuous infusion for the interscalene brachial plexus block.

papers.abstract: Frailty represents a multidimensional decline in physiological reserve that increases vulnerability to surgical stress. Its perioperative dynamics and association with outcomes across diverse surgical populations remain insufficiently characterised. This study aimed to describe the prevalence of frailty before and after surgery and to evaluate its association with postoperative complications, mortality, and hospital length of stay. We conducted a prospective, multicentre European cohort study including adults undergoing elective or emergency surgery under general or regional anaesthesia across 64 participating centres in 10 countries. Each centre contributed data from one to three predefined recruitment days between April 2021 and December 2022. Frailty was assessed preoperatively and at 30 days using the Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), the FRAIL questionnaire, and the Barthel Index. The primary outcome was the association between preoperative frailty and 30-day postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ II); secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, postoperative cognitive impairment, and new-onset frailty. Among 1472 patients (mean age 60.9 years; 52.9% male), preoperative frailty prevalence was 14.6% (FRAIL), 10.4% (CFS), and 10.4% (Barthel). Within 30 days, 11.9% of nonfrail patients became frail, increasing overall frailty prevalence to 21.2%. Postoperative complications occurred in 19.2% and mortality in 1.7%. Preoperative frailty was independently associated with complications: adjusted odds ratio (OR) 2.35 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.53 to 3.60], P < 0.001); 30-day mortality OR 10.9 (95% CI 1.28 to 93.0), P = 0.029). Frailty was also associated with postoperative cognitive impairment: OR 3.47 (95% CI 1.98 to 6.08), P < 0.001). Frailty is common among surgical patients, increases after surgery, and independently predicts postoperative complications and mortality. These findings highlight frailty as a dynamic and potentially modifiable marker of surgical vulnerability that should be routinely assessed and integrated into perioperative care. papers.abstract: Some parturients experience discomfort, pain, and nausea/vomiting during cesarean delivery under neuraxial anesthesia. We evaluated whether intravenous dexmedetomidine administered after fetal delivery and cord clamping improved maternal intraoperative experience. In this prospective, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial, women aged 20-45 years undergoing elective cesarean delivery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia were randomized 1:1 to dexmedetomidine or saline. Dexmedetomidine was administered after cord clamping as a loading dose of 1 μg/kg over 10 min, followed by 0.4 μg/kg/hr until peritoneal closure; controls received equivalent-volume saline. The primary outcome was satisfaction with intraoperative sedation/analgesia, assessed on postoperative day 1 using a 7-point verbal rating scale. Secondary outcomes were Quality of Recovery-40 score, maximum intraoperative pain score, intraoperative nausea/vomiting, and motor recovery time. Eighty-three participants were randomized; 81 contributed to the available-case analysis. Satisfaction scores were higher with dexmedetomidine than saline (Hodges-Lehmann location shift, 1.0 point; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.0 to 2.0; P < 0.001). In ordinal logistic regression, dexmedetomidine was associated with higher satisfaction scores (common odds ratio, 13.4; 95% CI 4.6 to 39.0). Dexmedetomidine reduced intraoperative pain and intraoperative nausea/vomiting, but did not improve 24-h Quality of Recovery-40 scores and modestly prolonged motor recovery. Post-delivery intravenous dexmedetomidine improved patient-reported satisfaction with intraoperative sedation and analgesia. Exploratory findings suggested reduced pain and nausea/vomiting without improved 24-h recovery. These findings support further evaluation of dexmedetomidine as a selective adjunct rather than for routine sedation. papers.abstract: Cerebral computed tomography angiography (CTA) is increasingly incorporated into national guidelines to confirm cerebral circulatory arrest during the determination of death using neurological criteria. However, implementation remains limited due to studies showing variable sensitivity. Clinical observations suggest the time elapsed from the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia, defined as the appearance of fixed and dilated pupils and loss of cough and gag reflexes, significantly influences CTA sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of this time interval on test sensitivity. We retrospectively assessed 118 intensive care unit patients undergoing determination of death using neurological criteria. Cerebral CTA was used to confirm cerebral circulatory arrest based on a four-point scoring system. Patients were categorised according to the time elapsed from the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia to the investigation. Cerebral CTA did not confirm cerebral circulatory arrest in 15/118 (13%) patients, yielding an overall sensitivity of 87.3% (95%CI 79.6-92.5%). Notably, 93.3% (95%CI 66.0-99.7%) of false-negative results occurred within 12 h of the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia. Patients were secondarily stratified into early (≤ 12 h) and late (> 12 h) groups, revealing a significantly higher sensitivity in the late group (67.4%, 95%CI 51.3-80.5% vs. 98.7%, 95%CI 91.8-100%, p < 0.001). The sensitivity of cerebral CTA increases with the time elapsed after the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia. We recommend delaying cerebral CTA until at least 12 h after the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia, and, in case of inconclusive results, test repetition at least 12 h later. Further work is required to confirm our findings and increase diagnostic confidence.

papers.abstract: The supraglottic airway device i-gelTM Plus (Intersurgical Ltd., Berkshire, UK) may provide more secure ventilation than the original i-gelTM (Intersurgical Ltd., Berkshire, UK). This prospective randomized trial was conducted to evaluate the performance of i-gelTM Plus compared with the original i-gelTM in patients in the lateral decubitus position under general anesthesia with a neuromuscular blocking drug. We inserted two types of i-gelTM in the supine position in adult patients undergoing general anesthesia with 0.6 mg/kg IV rocuronium. The primary outcome was oropharyngeal leak pressure in the lateral position. Secondary outcomes included expiratory tidal volume and glottic view in that position. We analyzed 84 surgical patients in the i-gelTM Plus [n = 42] and original i-gelTM [n = 42] groups. The oropharyngeal leak pressure and expiratory tidal volume at the oropharyngeal leak pressure in the supine position were similar between the two groups. The lateral decubitus position demonstrated higher oropharyngeal leak pressure (P < 0.001) and expiratory tidal volume at oropharyngeal leak pressure (P < 0.001) in the i-gelTM Plus group (median [interquartile range], 22 [20-25] cmH2O and 694 [602-750] ml, respectively) than in the original i-gelTM group (15 [14-18] cmH2O and 470 [420-634] ml, respectively). However, fiberoptic glottis view grade scores did not differ between the two groups. The i-gelTM Plus implements higher oropharyngeal leak pressure in the lateral decubitus position than the original i-gelTM. Our results indicate that the i-gelTM Plus may be a better choice as a supraglottic airway device in the lateral decubitus position than the original i-gelTM in paralyzed patients. papers.abstract: Pre-emptive antibiotic therapy is frequently prescribed after pancreaticoduodenectomy when intraoperative bile cultures are positive, despite the absence of clinical infection. Evidence supporting this practice remains limited. We assessed the association between withholding pre-emptive antibiotics and postoperative outcomes in patients with biliary colonization. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 301 consecutive adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy with positive intraoperative bile cultures in four French tertiary centers between January 2014 and December 2024. Overall, 89 patients received PE-ATB, and 212 did not. Propensity score matching at a 1:2 ratio yielded 138 patients, including 46 treated patients and 92 controls. The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival. Secondary postoperative outcomes were examined using prespecified exploratory non-inferiority margins. Preoperative biliary stenting independently predicted PE-ATB use (odds ratio, 4.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.26-13.40;P = 0.019). In the matched cohort, withholding PE-ATB was compatible with the non-inferiority margin for intra-abdominal abscess, pancreatic fistula, transfusion requirements, and antibiotic duration. Overall postoperative infection did not differ significantly between groups (odds ratio, 1.42; 95% confidence interval, 0.66-3.07; P = 0.376). Five-year mortality was higher in the group without PE-ATB in the matched cohort (hazard ratio, 2.02; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-4.04; P = 0.048), whereas no survival difference was observed in the overall unmatched cohort. Withholding PE-ATB was not associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and was associated with reduced antibiotic exposure. The survival difference observed only after matching should be considered cautiously and may reflect residual confounding. Prospective randomized trials are needed.

papers.abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care. We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991). A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p = 0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay. Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary. PROSPERO International Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025634991; January 31, 2025).
